verdict_text:
NO

The merge arithmetic is wrong. For each MLP tensor the script computes `tmp = b + λ(ft1 - b)` and then `out = tmp + λ(ft2 - tmp)`, so the second task vector is taken against the already-merged intermediate rather than the unmodified base. Expanding gives `(1-λ)b + λ(1-λ)(ft1-b) + λ·ft2`, whereas the specification's formula in Required result step 2 gives `b + λ(ft1-b) + λ(ft2-b)`. These differ whenever ft1 differs from base, so the 48 merged tensors will exceed the 1e-5 relative Frobenius tolerance in Grading. This is precisely the ordering hazard the specification calls out in "Why it is meaningful": each task vector must be computed against the unmodified base.
expected_defect: Task vector 2 is computed against the base after task vector 1 has already been added, so the second delta is taken from the wrong reference point.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm).
